question.text: A PM's registration certificate must be:

explanation.text: The Logic: A SEBI registration certificate is an official authorization to operate as a portfolio manager. Industry/regulatory practice expects the certificate (and the SEBI registration number) to be made visible to clients — typically by display at the registered office and inclusion in official communications — so that clients can readily verify the firm's regulated status. The remaining options reflect non-conformant practices. The Trap: Hiding the certificate, posting it on a stock exchange, or "burning after 10 years" all run counter to basic regulatory transparency. The certificate itself remains valid unless SEBI suspends or cancels it. Note: The specific requirement that the certificate be displayed at the registered office was not located in the cited pages of the NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers workbook (pages 126, 128, 131). The framing above reflects general industry/regulatory convention for SEBI-registered intermediaries rather than a direct workbook citation.
